Home page and product page ### Home — `/workspace/app/page.tsx` ```tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Home

Welcome to our store!

View Product
) } ``` - Sync Server Component (no data fetch) - Single client navigation entry: `next/link` → `/product` ### Product — `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` ```tsx import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' export default async function ProductPage() { const inventory = await getInventory() return (

Premium Widget

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } ``` - Async Server Component - Title is **static hardcoded string** `"Premium Widget"` — not fetched - Inventory (count/price) comes from `getInventory()` ### Layout — `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` ```tsx export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Shop', description: 'E-commerce product store', } ``` Document/tab title is `"Shop"`. The visible product title is the `

` on the product page, not metadata. --- ## 2. How navigation works ``` Home (/) --next/link--> /product ``` 1. User clicks `` 2. Next.js App Router does a **client-side soft navigation** (RSC flight request) 3. Server runs `ProductPage` as an async RSC 4. Response streams/returns the RSC payload; React commits the new tree There is no: - `loading.tsx` under `app/product/` - `` around inventory or the page - Prefetch customization on the `Link` - Client-side state or React Query / SWR Default `Link` prefetch still applies, but the product route is **dynamic** (see below), so prefetch cannot fully resolve a static shell of the finished page the way a pure static route would. --- ## 3. How the product title is fetched and rendered **It is not fetched.** The title is static JSX: ```tsx

Premium Widget

``` What *is* fetched is inventory only: ### `/workspace/lib/data.ts` ```tsx import { connection } from 'next/server' export async function getInventory() { await connection() return { count: Math.floor(Math.random() * 50), price: (Math.random() * 100).toFixed(2), } } ``` - `await connection()` marks this as **request-time / dynamic** (must wait for the actual request; cannot be fully prerendered as static) - Returns random `count` and `price` (no network I/O, but still gated behind `connection()`) ### Data flow for the visible title ``` Click Link → RSC request for /product → ProductPage() starts → await getInventory() → await connection() // dynamic boundary → return { count, price } → then render

Premium Widget

+ stock/price → HTML/RSC payload reaches client →

appears ``` The title is **blocked on inventory** even though it does not depend on it. --- ## 4. Loading states & data-fetching patterns | Pattern | Present? | |---------|----------| | SSR / RSC (async Server Components) | Yes — product page | | `connection()` dynamic API | Yes — forces dynamic | | `cacheComponents: true` | Yes — Cache Components / PPR-style | | `loading.tsx` | **No** | | React `Suspense` | **No** | | Client `useEffect` / SWR / fetch | **No** | | Streaming static shell vs dynamic hole | **Not structured** — whole page awaits | | `generateMetadata` for product title | **No** | With Cache Components enabled, Next can prerender a static shell and stream dynamic holes **only if** the tree is split (static content outside Suspense; dynamic work inside). Here the **entire page component** awaits dynamic data first, so nothing (including the title) can stream early. --- ## 5. What makes navigation feel slow / title not immediate ### Root cause `ProductPage` is a single async function that: ```tsx const inventory = await getInventory() // blocks entire render return (

Premium Widget

// static, but still waits ...
) ``` So: 1. Soft nav starts → server must run the full async page. 2. `getInventory()` → `connection()` forces dynamic, request-time work. 3. Until that resolves, **no product UI is produced**, including the static `

`. 4. No `loading.tsx` / Suspense fallback → blank (or old page) until the full RSC payload arrives. 5. Title only appears when the whole page is ready. ### Why Cache Components does not help as written `cacheComponents: true` wants a **static shell + dynamic holes**. That requires structure like: - Static title outside the await / outside a Suspense boundary - Dynamic inventory inside `` Current structure collapses static and dynamic into one blocking await at the page root. ### Secondary factors - No route-level `loading.tsx` for instant pending UI - No Suspense fallback for inventory - Dynamic `connection()` means the route cannot be fully static; every visit hits the server for inventory - Title is not in `metadata` / `generateMetadata` either, so even the document title does not show “Premium Widget” early --- ## Relevant patterns (as they exist today) **Navigation** ```tsx // app/page.tsx View Product ``` **Blocking page-level data fetch** ```tsx // app/product/page.tsx export default async function ProductPage() { const inventory = await getInventory() // gates entire page including title return ( /* title + inventory UI */ ) } ``` **Dynamic data boundary** ```tsx // lib/data.ts export async function getInventory() { await connection() // request-time; not fully static return { count: ..., price: ... } } ``` **Cache Components flag (unused effectively for shell streaming)** ```ts // next.config.ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } ``` --- ## Summary | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | Framework | Next.js App Router 16 (canary) + React 19 | | Home → product | `next/link` soft navigation to `/product` | | Product title source | Hardcoded `"Premium Widget"` in the product page RSC | | Title fetch? | No — static text | | Why title is late | Page `await`s dynamic `getInventory()` before returning any JSX | | Loading UI | None (`loading.tsx` / Suspense missing) | | Performance feature present but not leveraged | `cacheComponents: true` without static/dynamic split | **Main reason the title does not appear immediately:** the static product title is rendered only *after* a dynamic `await getInventory()` at the top of the page component, with no Suspense or `loading.tsx` to show a shell or fallback while inventory loads. session_id: ses_0bcdba672ffeDRDN8YuqclEW2P
